chains.title: TCF7L2-associated enhancer effect on POU5F1B
chains.element: rs6983267 lies in the pELS cCRE EH38E3858447, a candidate enhancer.
chains.cell_type: Colorectal cancer cells; HCT116 is the directly supported occupancy context.

links.claim: TCF7L2 is a plausible, not uniquely established, TF candidate: it is expressed and occupies the variant in HCT116, and a LEF1-mapped QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger binding to ref G than alt T at a strong modeled site. This is not a TCF7L2-specific QBiC-SELEX result.
The variant lies in pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; the reported chromatin maxima do not establish activity specifically in HCT116.

POU5F1B is a candidate target based on a T-increasing transverse-colon eQTL and gene-prioritization/TWAS evidence, but a direct link from this cCRE to POU5F1B is not shown. The eQTL direction would be compatible with the predicted lower TCF7L2 binding on T only if TCF7L2 represses POU5F1B; that regulatory sign is not established here.
TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant is reported in HCT116; this supports that cell line as a test context, not a general claim about colorectal tumors or normal colon.

rs6983267 is associated with colorectal cancer, and POU5F1B has been reported to promote CRC-cell proliferation and metastatic potential; the supplied evidence does not show that this variant acts through POU5F1B.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 occupancy at the site should favor G over T in HCT116, if the mapped QBiC-SELEX result reflects TCF7L2 binding there.
If this binding difference mediates the reported POU5F1B eQTL, T should increase POU5F1B relative to G; this requires a repressive effect of TCF7L2 that has not been demonstrated.
Editing the variant or perturbing TCF7L2 should alter POU5F1B regulation more than MYC regulation under this chain.
falsified_if: A sensitive allele-specific assay finds no G-favored TCF7L2 occupancy, or finds greater occupancy on T.
Precise editing or TCF7L2 perturbation has no effect on POU5F1B expression or enhancer activity in a relevant colorectal model.
The element reproducibly regulates MYC but not POU5F1B.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: The G/T substitution has no reproducible TF-mediated effect on enhancer activity or target-gene expression in relevant colorectal cells.
The CRC association may reflect linkage to another causal variant or a mechanism not mediated by TF binding at this base.
falsified_if: Precise G/T editing reproducibly changes TF occupancy and enhancer activity, with the effect depending on perturbation of the implicated TF.
The edited site produces a consistent allele-dependent change in a linked gene in a relevant colorectal model.

The variant lies in pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; the reported chromatin maxima do not establish activity specifically in HCT116.
POU5F1B is a candidate target based on the transverse-colon eQTL and gene-prioritization/TWAS evidence, but direct regulation by this element is unshown.

predictions: If SRF binding at this base mediates the effect, allele-specific SRF occupancy should favor G over T and SRF perturbation should reduce the allele-dependent POU5F1B effect.
The POU5F1B effect should depend more on SRF than on TCF7L2, distinguishing this chain from H1.
Because the modeled SRF site is weak, a robust absence of allele-specific SRF occupancy would weigh strongly against this chain.
falsified_if: Allele-specific assays find no SRF difference at the base or find greater occupancy on T.
SRF perturbation leaves the variant-dependent POU5F1B effect unchanged while TCF7L2 perturbation removes it.
Editing the variant does not alter POU5F1B expression or element activity in a relevant colorectal model.

In the post-GWAS analyses, we first identified new genome-wide significant associations: three genomic risk loci were identified at 8q24.21 (rs6983267, P = 6.98 × 10-12), 15q13.3 (rs58658771, P = 1.40 × 10-10), and 18q21.1 (rs6507874, P = 1.91 × 10-14).

In addition, the TWAS also identified four loci statistically significantly associated with CRC risk, largely explained by expression regulation, including six candidate genes (DUSP10, POU5F1B, C11orf53, COLCA1, COLCA2, and GREM1-AS1).

Here, upon characterizing cancer-specific transposable element-driven transpochimeric gene transcripts (TcGTs) produced by this tumor in the SYSCOL cohort, we find that expression of the hominid-restricted retrogene POU5F1B through aberrant activation of a primate-specific endogenous retroviral promoter is a strong negative prognostic biomarker.
Correlating this observation, we demonstrate that POU5F1B fosters the proliferation and metastatic potential of CRC cells.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr8:127401060:G>T, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000971), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 64 occupied (19 with a strong site), 5 of 133 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 6 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 497 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 6 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
